subject: Pricing & SKU packaging for private offer — NorthBridge
messages:
From: Maya Ramesh <maya.ramesh@northbridge.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northbridge.io
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Consolidated SKU and channel uplift model for private offer

Hi Sofia / Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has asked us to put a consolidated private offer together for our EMEA rollout. High level ask: we want a single billable SKU (reserved capacity bundle) with optional metered addons, and an explicit reseller uplift so our channel partners get a predictable margin.

Attached are two artifacts to start: NorthBridge_PO_Specs.pdf (requirements) and mvp_pricing_sheet.xlsx (current target numbers). We need to understand:
- Whether Redwood can deliver a blended list price + committed discount for a single SKU across AWS & GCP marketplace listings,
- How channel margin is expressed on the invoice (pass-through vs. separate commission), and
- Any constraints that would force SKU unbundling (billing, tax, or marketplace SKU limits).

Timing: Procurement would like a proposal by EOD Tuesday (2026-09-14) so we can include it in internal vendor shortlisting.

Can you confirm feasibility and a recommended packaging approach? If you have an internal mapping template we can fill that would speed things up.

Best,
Maya Ramesh
Head of Vendor Sourcing
NorthBridge Health

Attachments: NorthBridge_PO_Specs.pdf, mvp_pricing_sheet.xlsx

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramesh <maya.ramesh@northbridge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Consolidated SKU and channel uplift model for private offer

Maya — thanks for the brief and attachments. We can do a consolidated offering, but there are three tractable ways to structure it. I outline them below with the tradeoffs so procurement can pick what matters most.

Option A — Blended private SKU (recommended for procurement simplicity)
- Single reserved SKU that maps to a single private-offer listing in each marketplace.
- Commit discount applied at deal level; metered addons billed separately.
- Channel uplift handled as a separate invoice line item (explicit pass-through) — easiest for partner accounting.
- Pros: single invoice, simple onboarding. Cons: slightly less granular telemetry for internal product meter reconciliation.

Option B — Consolidated list price + reseller voucher
- Marketplace shows base SKU and we issue reseller vouchers/credits to partners for margin.
- Pros: maintains SKU-level metrics. Cons: voucher workflows increase operational ops and can delay payout.

Option C — SKU unbundling by marketplace (least preferred)
- Separate SKUs per cloud (AWS/GCP) to match marketplace constraints. Channel uplift is baked into reseller pricing.
- Pros: clear billing per cloud. Cons: procurement loses single-catalog simplicity.

Numbers and guardrails I suggest (benchmarks we use internally):
- Blended committed discount range: 18–28% off published list depending on commit term.
- Channel uplift (pass-through) typical floor: 10% recommended, 12–15% for strategic partners.
- If procurement requires reseller-protected netback, we recommend an escrow or invoice-routing flow (Irene can advise on mechanics).

Next steps I propose:
1) I will pull a draft SKU mapping and proposed list/commit numbers for NB-2026-0951 and share by Monday EOD.
2) Ben: can you confirm preferred floor for reseller margin and whether partner compensation is lump-sum or percent-of-revenue?
3) Irene: please propose the invoice-routing/escrow playbook for pass-through in EMEA and note any tax limitations.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call Monday to walk procurement through the options if helpful.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Consolidated SKU and channel uplift model for private offer

Maya / Sofia — attaching a preliminary SKU mapping (sku-mapping.csv) and a short ops runbook for EU invoice-routing. Summary of proposed mechanics: 

1) SKU mapping
- Core reserved bundle -> single private-offer SKU in AWS and GCP marketplaces. Marketplace metadata flags an "RB" (reserved bundle) so we can correlate usage. Metered addons are separate SKUs and billed as usage.

2) Channel margin handling
- We recommend Option A with explicit pass-through invoice line: Redwood invoices NorthBridge for gross revenue; a single line called "Partner Uplift" is created and routed to the partner as a credit memoby the partner's tax profile.
- Technical constraints: AWS marketplace supports a partner uplift via invoice memo; GCP requires a mapped reseller account for netback. Both are supported but require paperwork (reseller enrollment).

3) Legal & tax notes
- For EMEA, VAT handling requires that the reseller be registered in the invoiced country or we must issue VAT-inclusive pricing and rely on partner reclaim flows. We should not bake VAT into the uplift percent.

4) Proposed numbers for NB-2026-0951 (draft; can be tuned)
- Blended list price (per reserved unit): $1,200/mo
- Committed discount: 22% (annual 12-month commit)
- Partner uplift (pass-through): 12% floor, with authorization to increase to 15% for certified integrators.

Deliverables I can attach for procurement: 
- sku-mapping.csv (attached)
- ops-runbook-eu-invoice-routing.pdf (I will send after quick review)

Next steps: Sofia will produce the formal table for hubspot/deal record and I will draft the minimal contract language for the reseller uplift line and DocuSign link. If procurement signs off on the 12% floor, we can generate the private-offer documents and request reseller enrollment paperwork.

Irene Choi
Deal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
